statement: Show that $\tan(A+B)=\dfrac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}$, and hence find the exact value of $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{12}$.
solution:
Using $\tan(A+B)=\dfrac{\sin(A+B)}{\cos(A+B)}$ with the addition formulae,
$$\tan(A+B)=\frac{\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B}{\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B}=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}$$
after dividing numerator and denominator by $\cos A\cos B$.

Now $\dfrac{\pi}{12}=45^\circ-30^\circ$, so
$$\tan\frac{\pi}{12}=\frac{1-\frac1{\sqrt3}}{1+\frac1{\sqrt3}}=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{\sqrt3+1}.$$
Rationalising,
$$\frac{(\sqrt3-1)^2}{3-1}=\frac{3-2\sqrt3+1}{2}=2-\sqrt3.$$
